hypothesis: MC-002, MC-003, MC-004 and MC-056 jointly define a faithful, internally consistent and candidate-independent current MC-1 domain/precision/workload contract without narrowing the supported lathe/fixed-axis-three-axis-mill tranche or weakening inherited semantics.
falsification_criteria: an admitted MC-002 operation is absent from the frozen MC-004 denominator
an admitted constructor lacks finite exact source semantics required by MC-003
a provider or candidate can redefine physical validity, the denominator, the accuracy request or the resource envelope
a current-scope product boundary remains ambiguous after this integration review
legacy journal/body/provenance meaning is reinterpreted in place
the review claims native geometry, constructive completeness, STEP qualification or practical scale evidence that was not executed

domain_lock.history_model: finite ordered histories may include explicit re-clamp/re-chuck, non-cutting reorientation and lathe-to-mill-to-lathe transitions while preserving durable body identity and a common workpiece frame

product_boundary_resolutions.basis: The current MC-1 tranche is explicitly conventional lathe plus fixed-axis three-axis mill. Simultaneously controlled compound turn-mill/live-tool kinematics are not added as a third compound-machine process class. A workpiece achievable through the admitted lathe, mill, re-clamp and machine-transition history remains in scope; this decision does not permit a provider to reject any of the 26 frozen operations or equivalent admitted histories.

The current MC-1 tranche defines conventional single-workpiece lathe/mill process semantics with explicit re-clamp/re-chuck and cross-machine histories. Simultaneously coordinated multi-spindle/transfer-machine process semantics are future machine-module scope. A workpiece achievable through the admitted finite history remains in scope; throughput-oriented machine coordination is not silently promoted into a new mandatory constructor family.

po01.title: Domain fidelity
po01.reason: The current MC-1 machine/process boundary, operation denominator, physical-validity rules, exact source semantics and candidate-independent request profile are explicit, mutually consistent and protected against solver/provider narrowing. Product boundaries that were intentionally left open by MC-002 are resolved here from programme authority without removing any previously admitted operation.
po01.scope_limit: PO-01 accepts the current MC-1 domain contract only; it does not prove a terminating constructive geometry route or implementation correctness.

basis: faithful process-first domain and physical-validity contract from MC-002
exact/versioned numeric, curve, transform and phase source semantics from MC-003
candidate-independent frozen workload, accuracy, hardware and resource request from MC-004
MC-005 product-boundary resolution and cross-contract consistency review

claims_not_made: no constructive completeness or termination proof (MC-B remains NOT_ESTABLISHED)
no conventional B-rep/STEP representability or independent-consumer qualification
no production bootstrap or paid/native execution authorization
future_scope_rule: Adding continuous five-axis cutting, compound simultaneous turn-mill/live-tool kinematics, coordinated multi-spindle transfer semantics, additive processes or other new process classes requires a prospective reviewed domain-contract revision and corresponding workload/profile revision before candidate testing. It may not retroactively alter this MC-A evidence or convert a candidate failure into an exclusion.
